abstract_sentences.text: We study the computational cost of differential privacy in terms of memory efficiency.
While the trade-off between accuracy and differential privacy is well-understood, the inherent cost of privacy regarding memory use remains largely unexplored.
abstract_sentences.connection: narrows the scope to a missing memory trade-off

abstract_sentences.text: This paper establishes for the first time an unconditional space lower bound for user-level differential privacy by introducing a novel proof technique based on a multi-player communication game.
abstract_sentences.connection: answers the stated gap with a proof framework

evidence.anchor: novel proof technique based on a multi-player communication game

abstract_sentences.text: Central to our approach, this game formally links the hardness of low-memory private algorithms to the necessity of contribution capping—tracking and limiting the users who disproportionately impact the dataset.
abstract_sentences.connection: supplies the mechanism behind the framework

abstract_sentences.text: We demonstrate that winning this communication game requires transmitting information proportional to the number of over-active users, which translates directly to memory lower bounds.
abstract_sentences.connection: turns the mechanism into a communication-to-space bridge

evidence.anchor: translates directly to memory lower bounds

abstract_sentences.text: We apply this framework, as an example, to the fundamental problem of estimating the number of distinct elements in a stream and we prove that any private algorithm requires almost Ω̃(T^{1/3}) space to achieve certain error rates in a promise variant of the problem.

This resolves an open problem in the literature (by Jain et al. (Jain et al., 2023a) and Cummings et al. (Cummings et al., 2025)) and establishes the first exponential separation between the space complexity of private algorithms and their non-private Õ(1) counterparts for a natural statistical estimation task.
abstract_sentences.connection: elevates the instance result to a literature and separation claim

abstract_sentences.text: Furthermore, we show that this communication-theoretic technique generalizes to broad classes of problems, yielding lower bounds for private medians, quantiles, and max-select.

evidence.anchor: yielding lower bounds for private medians

final_judgment.single_storyline: A recurring heavy-user set C must be remembered to cap contributions; the paper turns that intuition into AvoidHeavyHitters communication, then turns any accurate low-space DP stream algorithm into a low-communication protocol. [p.2 §1: essentially necessary; p.6-8 §2.3-§3.3]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: It keeps task/DP definitions, occurrency and prior capping, the four-step hard instance, game rules, core lemmas/corollary, correlation intuition, Theorems 2.1-2.3, and the conclusion. [p.3-8]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: It moves concentration, usefulness coupling, encoding proof, and full extension gadgets to A.1-A.4; strict verification of those lemmas depends on the appendix, while the main theorem chain remains visible in the body. [p.6 §3; p.11-13 Appendix]
final_judgment.best_pattern: The prose first makes capping concrete in CountDistinct, states an independently understandable game, then makes algorithm memory equal protocol message in Corollary 3.3. [p.4-8 §2.1-§3.3]
final_judgment.largest_gap: The named extensions are proved, yet broader future applicability remains belief language. The abstract separately names medians but no median theorem is titled; the main text also leaves the (2w,k) construction-to-(w,k) theorem constant rescaling implicit and defers full probability proofs. [p.1; p.5; p.6; p.8]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a lower bound whose mechanism is remembering a set of persistent influential entities, encode the carried memory as a multi-player message and prove a communication lower bound under a game success constraint. [p.7 §3.1-§3.2]
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This paper proves that rule only for its continual-release, user-level DP, promise/parameter regime and a fingerprinting-plus-rounding bridge; it does not establish it for arbitrary privacy models, streams, or deployed systems. [p.3 §2; p.5 Theorem 2.1; p.13 A.4]
